about: The kinds of road (the Ledger topic 'Buildings and works', your note on 'Which kinds of road': split by material, and hence speed and bandwidth; railways are not roads and come separately). 'pace' is the share of the ground's marching cost left on the road (lower is faster, whatever the ground); 'trade' is the share added to the trade of the provinces it crosses; 'reach' is how much of a far province's distance penalty a road to the capital takes away; 'cost' is talents per km and 'workers' men per km taken from manpower while it is built; 'requires' is the technology that opens it. Building takes years by length: 100 km a year, faster as the realm learns transport and construction (your note on 'What a road costs'). Our own figures, free for any use. 'canals' are dug the same way, between two waters (sea or a river) (your answer 'History's own plus any canal you draw between two waters'): ships pass through them; without the pound lock (1373) a canal can't climb hills (ground rougher than 'max_rugged'). 'walls' are frontier walls, drawn point to point along your land (your answers on frontier walls): an army of another realm (not an ally) crossing one loses 'cross_km' of its march for each crossing; each needs 'garrison' men a km held from manpower once finished, or it decays like an unpaid road; provinces it runs through are better held ('province_garrison'). Stopping raids waits on raiding (the campaign question 'Raids').

kinds.name: Earth road
kinds.description: A cleared and levelled track: passable in summer, mud in winter.

kinds.name: Gravel road
kinds.description: A road of packed gravel on a bed of stones (via glareata strata).

kinds.name: Paved stone road
kinds.description: Fitted stone blocks on deep foundations, drained and surveyed straight (via silice strata), as the Via Appia was paved from 295 BC.

kinds.name: Macadam road
kinds.description: McAdam's layers of broken stone, cambered to shed the rain.

kinds.name: Asphalt road
kinds.description: Asphalt and concrete for motor traffic.

canals.name: Canal
canals.description: A cut between two waters on level ground, like Necho's canal or the Fossa Drusiana.

canals.name: Canal with locks
canals.description: Pound locks lift boats over the hills, like the Canal du Midi.

canals.name: Ship canal
canals.description: Wide and deep enough for seagoing ships, like Suez and Kiel.

walls.name: Ditch and rampart
walls.description: A ditch and an earth rampart with watchtowers, like the Fossatum Africae or the Antonine Wall.

walls.name: Stone wall
walls.description: A stone curtain with forts and milecastles, like Hadrian's Wall or the Anastasian Wall.
